title: observability: token-level KV metrics, cost/latency dashboards + alert tuning
author: Priya Kapoor
release_notes: Add token-level KV cache metrics and cost/latency dashboards; tune alerts for cost regressions and KV cache degradation; ship behind feature flag with gradual rollout; no user-facing API changes.
body: Context: We need better observability into per-token cost and latency drivers to diagnose regressions in serving economics. This PR adds token-level KV cache metrics, per-model token cost attribution, Grafana dashboards for cost and latency breakdowns, and tuned alert rules that reduce noise while catching regressions (cache hit rate drops, cost-per-1k-token increases, sudden latency p50/p95 spikes). Motivation: recent incidents showed high token-level cost with subtle KV cache pollution; current dashboards only surfaced aggregate RPS and cost which delayed root cause diagnosis. Summary of changes: 1) metrics: new metrics exported from the serving runtime: redwood_kv_cache_token_hits_total, redwood_kv_cache_token_misses_total, redwood_token_cost_usd_total (counter by model, variant, region, customer_tier), redwood_token_latency_ms_bucket (histogram by model/route); 2) attribution: a lightweight per-request post-processor that records token-level cost attribution using model unit-price metadata and KV hit/miss tags; 3) dashboards: Grafana panels showing cost/latency breakdown by token position, model, and KV hit/miss, and a new "Token Economics" dashboard that surfaced cost-per-1k-tokens over time with drilldowns; 4) alerts: new alert rules with recovery windows and noise reduction (e.g. alert on 15m increase >20% cost-per-1k over 3h baseline, or KV miss rate >5% sustained for 10m on Dedicated pools); 5) rollout: feature-flagged and started with 10% canary traffic, 50% after 24h, full rollout after KPIs stable; 6) docs: observability docs and runbook updates for investigating token-economics alerts; 7) tests: unit tests for metric labels and integration test exercising dashboard queries against synthetic traces. Checklist: - [x] Metrics added and exported with stable label sets - [x] Dashboards implemented and reviewed - [x] Alerts tuned with recovery windows and noise filters - [x] Feature flag + canary rollout plan - [x] Docs and runbook updated - [x] CI: unit + integration tests passing Files changed (high-level): - serving/metrics/kv_metrics_collector.go: add token-level counters, label normalization - serving/attribution/token_cost_attributor.go: cost attribution module and config - grafana/dashboards/token_economics.json: new dashboard JSON - monitoring/alerts/token_economics.rules: Prometheus alert rules with recording rules - webapp/src/routes/dashboards/TokenEconomics.jsx: dashboard frontend and drilldowns - docs/observability/token-economic-metrics.md: docs and runbook - ci/testdata/token_econ_synthetic.yaml: synthetic traces for integration tests Testing: Ran unit tests locally and on CI. Integration tests run via perf-canary job; initial flaky query fixed by increasing query window and the CI run passed after rerun. Rollout: started feature flag at 10% on Dedicated and Hosted, monitored token-econ dashboard and KV miss rates, promoted to 50% after 24h, then to 100% after 72h with no regressions. Backout plan: disable feature flag and revert metrics-only flag if unexpected cost spikes appear; alert runbook points to disabling attribution/collection for troubleshooting. Backwards compatibility: Metrics use new metric names (prefixed) and stable label sets; no breaking API changes. Notes: we intentionally avoid emitting per-token payloads to logs to protect PII. See linked Linear tickets for follow-ups (ENG-3421: batch-level aggregation support, SRE-128: alerting escalations).

review_comments: Jordan Lee: Can we avoid high-cardinality labels for customer_id? Priya: We only include customer_tier and a hashed customer_id with low-cardinality buckets behind an opt-in flag.
Alex Chen: Alert thresholds look aggressive for hosted; suggest 30% for hosted. Priya: lowered hosted thresholds and added a 3h baseline window for trend detection.
Samantha Ortiz: Confirmed dashboards render on smaller clusters; added an integration test that queries recording rules rather than raw metrics.
Jordan Lee: CI flaky on prometheus query assertion fixed by increasing window; re-ran CI and all checks passed.
short_description: Adds token-level KV cache metrics + cost attribution, dashboards, and tuned alerts to make token economics diagnosable and actionable.
